title: Stable SNAP receipt coexists with different annual child-care payment, assistance, and work-constraint profiles
source_unit: Identified SIPP person with November-to-December adjacent SNAP status and annual fall child-care fields

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November no SNAP to December no SNAP; annual child-care fields

denominator.unit: valid person-transition records for care-prevented-work outcome; payment outcomes n=1783

observations.method: Official Census SIPP 2025 reference-year slice; November-to-December SNAP status transition paired to December-recorded annual fall child-care fields; November WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay factor 0.5 used by scripts/analyze_sipp_snap_transition_childcare_bridge.py.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive Fay-BRR estimates; each child-care field has its own valid universe. Annual fall fields are not monthly December outcomes and no causal program effect is estimated.
observations.subgroup: Persons with stable nonreceipt from November to December; records with invalid or out-of-universe child-care fields are excluded from that measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Stable nonreceipt may reflect different household composition, eligibility, employment, income, care arrangements, or unobserved need rather than program protection.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; November SNAP to December SNAP; annual child-care fields

denominator.unit: valid person-transition records for care-prevented-work outcome; payment outcomes n=259

observations.method: Same SIPP transition and Fay-BRR procedure as the adjacent observation, for continued SNAP receipt.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive Fay-BRR estimates with wider intervals in the smaller stable-receipt cell; annual fall fields are not monthly December outcomes and no causal program effect is estimated.
observations.subgroup: Persons with SNAP receipt in both November and December; records with invalid or out-of-universe child-care fields are excluded from that measure.
observations.counterinterpretation: Continued receipt may identify households with greater measured or unmeasured need, children, work constraints, or eligibility complexity; higher assistance/work-constraint shares cannot be read as effects of receipt.

boundary: This is a same-person adjacent-month status comparison with annual fall child-care measures. The sparse November-to-December entry and exit cells are not promoted as reliable estimates. The result does not observe notice, route effort, benefit amount, child-care quality, exact monthly timing, trust, or political action.
